note: The agent sessions of this harness and the only source of what runs (docs/AGENT-STACK.md). The fleet watchdog's schema - session_name, workdir, launch_cmd, enabled, cooldown_sec, env, note - plus the harness's keys: role, flag (the .env switch; when it is set it decides, enabled is the default), parent and task (the lineage the tmux-agent dashboard shows), charter (the session's CLAUDE.md), source and ref, cycle and cadence_sec (run by the supervisor in the workdir), notices (where a cycle's messages for agent come from), writes, cost, title, tile, page (the path on the home listener where its cycle's STATUS.html is served and its tile links) and agent_process (the command its pane runs while its agent is alive). /agent/spoke.sh reads and checks it.

sessions.task: the hub: plans, asks the spokes, starts workers, answers the person with sources
sessions.title: Agent
sessions.note: Started by startup.sh through /agent/tmux-session-start.sh. Its pane falls back to a shell when claude exits; the supervisor reports that and starts the session again only when it is gone.

sessions.task: starts the enabled spokes from the registry, starts again the ones that stop, reports stuck ones, makes only safe repairs, records every session's start and stop in the session ledger and closes a scratch session whose process has exited, its output kept; no model
sessions.title: Supervisor
sessions.note: A script that never calls a model. startup.sh runs /agent/supervisor.sh start: the loop runs detached, and this session shows its last pass. The container's keepalive runs /agent/supervisor.sh ensure every minute, which starts it again when its last pass is stale.

sessions.task: poll the configured Slack channels, classify and journal every message, keep the answered state true, hand agent each open ask, and stage replies to the outbox for the human GO - never send
sessions.cost: Slack read calls every cycle (60 s) and a token in .env.local; model tokens only when agent or the person talks to it
sessions.title: Conversations spoke
sessions.note: The communication engine at the charter's ref, cloned anonymously into its workdir's repo/. The ref is the engine's tag v0.1.0, the same commit install-comms.sh pins; the loopback Slack stub the loop's --stub-test needs came with v0.2.0, so that self-test does not run against it. On by default; with SLACK_BOT_TOKEN or SLACK_CHANNELS unset it waits for Slack: its session runs, its cycle does not.

sessions.task: mine new session transcripts into rule candidates through the gates, for a person to review and promote
sessions.cost: no model calls in its hourly cycle; model tokens only when agent or the person talks to it
sessions.title: Insights spoke
sessions.note: The vendored LogLearner runtime; it clones nothing.

sessions.task: read-only status of every configured Kubernetes context (nodes, allocatable and requested GPUs and EFA) and the broker of this harness's cluster lock: GPU leases, their queue and their expiry
sessions.cost: read-only kubectl calls every 15 minutes; needs a kubeconfig; model tokens only when agent or the person talks to it
sessions.title: Clusters spoke
sessions.note: Its loop is self-contained: nothing to clone. Its cycle also runs the GPU broker (broker.py beside the loop), which answers gpu-lease and gpu-release requests with leases of the harness's cluster lock (/agent/cluster-lock.sh) and reclaims the expired ones (docs/cluster-lock.md).

sessions.task: read the tmux-agent dashboard's census every cycle, keep one book of the sessions on the watched tmux server, tell agent what changed, and never act on a session
sessions.cost: loopback reads of the dashboard; model tokens only when agent or the person talks to it
sessions.title: Sessions spoke
sessions.note: Its charter is complete; the cycle script it specifies is not written yet, so the supervisor runs no cycle for it. It needs the dashboard tile on (UI_TMUX_AGENT=true).

sessions.task: keep the Loop Deck's registry, run evidence and page current for this harness's own loops, validate every refresh at the pinned data contract, and tell agent when a loop goes RED or the Deck stalls
sessions.cost: local reads every 60 s; model tokens only when agent or the person talks to it
sessions.title: Loops spoke
sessions.note: The vendored Loop Deck release tree.

sessions.task: triage the open issues and pull requests in scope - conflicts, failing checks, requested changes, what needs a reply - keep STATUS.md current, tell agent what changed, and stage reply drafts for a human GO - never post
sessions.cost: read-only GitHub calls every 15 minutes (about one per open item and one more per pull request) with GH_TOKEN set; without it it waits for GitHub; model tokens only when agent or the person talks to it
sessions.title: Issues spoke
sessions.note: Nothing posts from it: a draft reaches GitHub only through /agent/charters/issues/post.sh after a person's GO naming its sha256. Its cycle reads through a front that refuses every write. The vendored issues tracker at /opt/issues-tracker (VENDORED.md names its export; tools/vendor-issues-tracker.sh refreshes it) gives the cycle its front and, with no repository named, its scan; without an export that passed the harness's scans, the cycle uses its own scan and front. On by default; with GH_TOKEN unset it waits for GitHub: its session runs, its cycle does not.

sessions.task: build container images inside the harness through the stack's BuildKit daemon into its registry, keep the build doctrine, and keep the daemon, the registry, the build cache and the disk headroom in view - never push outside the stack
writes: the images it builds in the stack's registry
sessions.cost: local reads every 5 minutes (the daemon's socket, the stack's registry, the disk); a build pulls its base images and packages from the internet; model tokens only when agent or the person talks to it
sessions.title: Docker spoke
sessions.note: Its cycle and the build helper /agent/image-build.sh are self-contained: nothing to clone. Its build substrate, a rootless BuildKit daemon and a registry, runs as two sidecar containers that ./run.sh starts on the docker target with SPOKE_DOCKER=true (./docker.sh); on a target without them its cycle writes that there is none. Its tile opens its page, STATUS.md rendered by its cycle, at /docker/.

sessions.task: a timestamp every cycle and an answer to every question, proving the spoke scaffold end to end
sessions.cost: no model tokens per cycle (its loop is a shell script); its Claude Code session spends tokens only when someone talks to it
sessions.title: Example spoke
sessions.note: Synthetic: the way to see the scaffold work on a fresh harness without spending tokens on a loop.
